items.title: Fresh-clone exhaustive run: first ts-server boot fails on DECKO_MOD_PUBLIC_DIR (untracked mod/ dir)
items.assignment:
Fix GitHub issue 17 in KatsuJinCode/decko-ts: "Fresh-clone exhaustive run: first ts-server boot fails on DECKO_MOD_PUBLIC_DIR (untracked mod/ dir)".

Work in /data/home/decko-ts. Read its AGENTS.md first and follow it. Make the branch port/instabox-issue-17 from origin/deploy/full-candidate-20261104 (the port's working line; main is the old work board). Touch only that branch; other agents work on other branches. Nothing is ever sent or shown to anyone outside this repository.

The issue, in full:

What happened: in a fresh clone at the roll tip 4e0c569c (checkout C:/localProjects/decko-ts-journeys-rolled-20261024, branch journeys/regrade-rolled-20261024), the first ts-server boot attempt of run-exhaustive.mjs failed with 'Error: DECKO_MOD_PUBLIC_DIR has no mod/ directory: reference-harness/oracle/app/public' (ts-server.mjs:76 gate). The second attempt booted and served the whole run (1359 interactions, zero 5xx). The same first-boot failure was observed on the journeys/regrade-20261023 checkout (its .runtime/exhaustive/2026-10-23-bootfailure-modpublic-missing). Cause: reference-harness/oracle/app/public/mod carries 0 git-tracked files (git ls-files is empty there), so a fresh clone lacks it until setup populates it, and the boot gate fires before that. Cost: one failed boot attempt and a confusing stack trace at the start of every fresh-clone run; no grading effect observed (the retry boots and the run completes). How it could be better: stage or symlink the mod/ content from a tracked source before the first boot (or have startEngine verify and populate it), so a fresh clone boots first try.

Commit only the files you changed with git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>, through any commit hook (never --no-verify), and push only your branch: git push origin port/instabox-issue-17. Open no pull request. This is a Linux machine; the product may also ship on Windows, so do not change behaviour a Windows run depends on without saying so, and name any test you could not run here.

Report back in plain English: what you changed, the test results with counts, anything you could not verify on this machine, and the pushed commit.

items.title: Staging dist bootstrap checks module EXISTENCE but not CURRENCY, so a failed dist build surfaces as missing-module names
items.assignment:
Fix GitHub issue 16 in KatsuJinCode/decko-ts: "Staging dist bootstrap checks module EXISTENCE but not CURRENCY, so a failed dist build surfaces as missing-module names".

Work in /data/home/decko-ts. Read its AGENTS.md first and follow it. Make the branch port/instabox-issue-16 from origin/deploy/full-candidate-20261104 (the port's working line; main is the old work board). Touch only that branch; other agents work on other branches. Nothing is ever sent or shown to anyone outside this repository.

The issue, in full:

WHAT HAPPENED

The staging server's readiness gate (tests/card/auth/staging-server-dist-bootstrap.ts) checks that every dist module the server imports exists and is non-empty. It does not check that the content is current.

On 2026-10-23 a lane change to src/card/render/page.ts introduced twelve TypeScript narrowing errors. The gate's own build step (tsc -p tsconfig.json, the bootstrap's recipe) failed inside the suite's beforeAll, and the suites reported a wall of missing dist module names (dist/vendor/libsass-wasm/LICENSE and dozens of vendor paths) instead of the build error that actually caused them. The lane spent a cycle reading the wrong failure.

WHAT IT COST

One misdirected debugging cycle in the routes round-six lane, and a risk that lands on any lane that touches a file the staging server imports. A stale dist that is missing an export a server imports fails the same way at import time with a misleading error.

HOW IT COULD BE BETTER

Two gates, both small:

1. Currency: the readiness check should compare the dist module's content against its source (a build stamp, a content hash, or the source mtime against the dist mtime) and rebuild or fail loudly with the build output when the dist is stale, instead of letting a stale dist through and failing later at import time.

2. Failure surface: when the bootstrap's own tsc build fails, the error it raises should carry the build output (the bootstrap already collects result.stdout and result.stderr) and name the build failure, not the list of missing modules. Today the missing-module list is the dominant message even when the modules exist.

Reference: docs/reports/routes-round6-2026-10-23.md, the round receipt, section 'A defect found in the shared staging bootstrap'.

Open no pull request. This is a Linux machine; the product may also ship on Windows, so do not change behaviour a Windows run depends on without saying so, and name any test you could not run here.
